citations.quote: 2. **Performance status:** ECOG 3, primarily limited by dyspnea and fatigue.
Performance status has declined to ECOG 2.

candidates.description: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale used to assess how a patient's disease affects their daily living abilities.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numerical ECOG grade provided in the assessment or performance status section of the clinical note.
candidates.measurement_definition: Standard ECOG scale where 0 is fully active and 4 is completely disabled.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence does not provide the full criteria used for the classification in each specific case, only the resulting grade.

candidates.description: A calculated ratio of the absolute neutrophil count to the absolute lymphocyte count, often used as a marker of systemic inflammation.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify and extract the numeric value listed as 'NLR' or 'neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio' from laboratory data or baseline summaries.
candidates.measurement_definition: The quotient of the absolute neutrophil count divided by the absolute lymphocyte count, typically expressed as a decimal.
candidates.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR)
candidates.uncertainty: The exact timing of the blood draw relative to the 'baseline' is not consistently specified across all mentions.

limitations: Small number of patients with explicitly reported NLR values.
Limited variation in PD-L1 expression (consistently 10%) across multiple cases, reducing its utility as a modifier in this specific dataset.
Heterogeneity in histology (adenocarcinoma vs. squamous) is present but not quantified across a large enough cohort to establish a strong baseline trend.
summary: The evidence identifies variations in baseline functional status (ECOG) and inflammatory markers (NLR) among patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presenting with KRAS G12C mutations.
